# Matthew Paver Portfolio

> Public decision tools, data products and reproducible engineering case studies.

Site: https://matthewpaver.github.io/
Author: Matthew Paver
Based: London
Rule: do not invent adoption, customer, revenue or accuracy claims

## Projects

### PolicyLens

- Shelf: AI engineering
- Status: Public
- Problem: Reviewers can see a risky policy diff without proving which sensitive request became reachable
- Outcome: Turns an IAM policy diff into a cited stop or pass decision
- Proof: Published browser-local correction journey and JSON export; authored benchmark; AWS simulator cross-check not yet run
- Available now: Run the synthetic example in your browser. No account, install, upload or API key.
- Publication boundary: The product landing includes a three-stage review using the actual deterministic engine. The browser demo processes policies locally; account analysis and optional AI stay in the Node server.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=policylens
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/iam-policy-auditor
- Stack: Node.js, AWS IAM, AI evals, Docker

### ProjectLens

- Shelf: Products
- Status: Public
- Problem: A change pack can tell a different story from the schedule it cites
- Outcome: Gives a change board an evidence pack and decision record before approval
- Proof: Published evidence desk; three priorities and all findings retained; draft recovery; accountable decisions and exact source exports
- Available now: Runs in your browser. No account; sample schedules included.
- Publication boundary: The public product includes an interactive real-engine example, source evidence, narrative revision, local draft recovery, decisions and exports. Public-record context stays optional.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=projectlens
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/ProjectLens
- Stack: Browser JavaScript, Python, Playwright, optional Gemini RAG

### QuickSupply

- Shelf: Products
- Status: Public
- Problem: A Liverpool supply-cover booking journey relied on dated screens and manual follow-up
- Outcome: Makes a three-sided booking handoff visible and testable
- Proof: Recorded school, agency and teacher handoff; newer DfE context and audit fixes remain local work
- Available now: Watch the recorded prototype without installing anything.
- Publication boundary: Historical case study with fictional data. The public source is not a deployment-ready staffing service.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=quicksupply
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/QuickSupply
- Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle, SSE

### Winchester House Hunter

- Shelf: Products
- Status: Public
- Problem: A listing price omits commute, cash position, sold-price context and condition
- Outcome: Turns a property shortlist into an affordability and evidence review
- Proof: Nine seeded homes; hosted market summaries are illustrative until the traceable local rebuild is published
- Available now: Runs in your browser. No account; nine seeded homes.
- Publication boundary: The public homes, scores and market summaries are illustrative. A local rebuild now traces 931 included 2025 sales to a retained public source, but that provenance update has not been published yet.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=winchester
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/winchester-buyer-check
- Stack: Browser JavaScript, HTML and CSS, public data

### Marketing ML Lakehouse

- Shelf: Data systems
- Status: Public
- Problem: A notebook hides the source contracts and data checks needed to reproduce an analysis
- Outcome: Rebuilds campaign files into checked reporting tables
- Proof: Public console built from generated evidence; next-day model evaluated against a prior-day baseline
- Available now: Browser snapshot needs no setup. Python is required to rebuild the template.
- Publication boundary: The console, pipeline and next-day evaluation are published and rebuilt in CI. The optional GA4 public-data profile needs your own BigQuery access and is not part of the published results.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=lakehouse
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/marketing-ml-lakehouse
- Stack: Python, DuckDB, XGBoost, Streamlit, Makefile

### HR Performance Analytics

- Shelf: Analytics
- Status: Public
- Problem: A dashboard screenshot does not preserve the model, calculations or interpretation decisions
- Outcome: Explains corrections to a historical Power BI exercise
- Proof: Historical AdventureWorks dashboard; correction on the case page; public README and exports still need a rebuild
- Available now: Read the correction here. Power BI Desktop is needed to edit the historical report.
- Publication boundary: The corrected data and replacement review PDF are local, unpublished work. The public repository still contains historical interpretations. Refreshing and checking the original Power BI report remains outstanding.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=hr
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/hr-performance-dashboards
- Stack: Power BI, DAX, AdventureWorks, reporting

### Can England Win It

- Shelf: Finished experiments
- Status: Archived
- Problem: A one-event product loses its purpose when the event ends
- Outcome: Shows a transparent tournament scenario model and closes it when the event ends
- Proof: 10,000 seeded runs; model tests; live retrospective; POSTMORTEM.md
- Available now: Runs in your browser. No account or setup.
- Publication boundary: Finished entertainment experiment. Assumptions such as player boosts are part of the game, not validated sporting effects.
- Preview: https://matthewpaver.github.io/preview.html?app=england
- Repo: https://github.com/MatthewPaver/can-england-win-it
- Stack: TypeScript, React, Vite, Vitest
